newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian interior minister raps Chechnya over bomb.
newsitem.headline: Russian interior minister raps Chechnya over bomb.

text.p: Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov, blaming a bomb blast at a Russian railway station on Chechens, expressed fears on Tuesday that violence was spinning out of control in the north Caucasus area around rebel Chechnya.

Kulikov told reporters he feared separatist Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov was losing control and added: "If Maskhadov does not get rid of terrorists in his entourage, his regime will become a criminal one."

Kulikov, who is also a deputy prime minister, said police had detained two Chechen women fighters who he said had organised the explosion in the spa resort of Pyatigorsk on Monday which killed two and wounded more than 20 people.

He said the two were part of a Chechen armed group which attacked the Russian town of Budennovsk in 1995, staging a bloody hostage drama there. "These are not rebels. This is not a political struggle, this is banditry," he said vowing to catch and destroy those responsible.

Kulikov said the people of the north Caucasus had demanded that Moscow taken harsh measures against Chechen "bandits" and said there was a danger of pogroms against Chechens in Russia following what he called a series of "terrorist acts".
"The situation in north Caucasus is becoming extremely tense. I am afraid it could become uncontrollable, Chechen pogroms may start," he said.
